_about: The closed set of rules the review critics may judge against. A finding must cite a rule id from this file; anything else is inadmissible. Each rule points at the document that actually states it — this registry is an index, never the source. `.claude/hooks/rules.py check` (and tests/test_rules.py) proves every source file, anchor and excerpt still matches, so a spec edit that changes what a rule means fails the suite instead of rotting silently.
excerpt_note: excerpt_sha256 is the sha256 of the cited section's text — from its anchor line up to the next heading of the same level, whitespace-stripped. Regenerate deliberately with `rules.py reseal <id>` after confirming the rule still says what the registry claims.

rules.rule: Money is integer cents (int), never float. Quantities are whole ints.
rules.violation: A float, a `/`, or a `round()` producing a money value; a numpy dtype holding cents; money formatted outside ui/formatting.py.

rules.rule: Cost basis is inferred by a market-value-weighted split of net_consideration_in = cash_out + sum(cards out) - cash_in; the rounding residual goes to the largest-value line.
rules.violation: A basis derivation that drops the residual, reallocates it elsewhere, or reweights by anything other than market value.

rules.rule: Disposals draw down lots FIFO: within the cost group an outgoing card names, else across all of that item's lots. A named group is still consumed oldest-first.
rules.violation: A disposal path without a deterministic acquisition ordering, or a batching rewrite that loses it.

rules.rule: Transactions are never hard-deleted: soft-void plus an append-only audit_log; edit = atomic void + re-post. Sole sanctioned exception: delete_inventory_entry (ADR 2026-07-11).
rules.violation: A DELETE against transaction/transaction_line, or a state change with no audit_log row.

rules.rule: Intent is per-lot: personal | resale | ripping. Ripping lots are valued at $0 and are never sellable.
rules.violation: A valuation path that omits the ripping check, or a sell path that can reach a ripping lot.

rules.rule: Migrations are forward-only and append-only: add a new numbered file in data/migrations/, never edit a shipped one.
rules.violation: A modification to an existing file under data/migrations/, or a numbered migration aimed at a database other than inventory.db.

rules.rule: The domain and service layers are Qt-free and unit-testable headless.
rules.violation: A PySide6 import reaching src/tcginventory/domain/ or src/tcginventory/services/.

rules.rule: The UI never issues SQL and never does money math.
rules.violation: A conn.execute or raw SQL string under src/tcginventory/ui/, or arithmetic on cents in a view, model or delegate.

rules.rule: Invariant 1: the sum of lot.remaining_qty for an item equals the units currently on hand for that item.
rules.violation: An on-hand quantity derived from anything other than the sum over open lots, or a write that moves remaining_qty without a corresponding lot effect.

rules.rule: Invariant 2: for any `out` line, the sum of lot_consumption.quantity equals transaction_line.quantity.
rules.violation: A disposal writing a line without consuming lots to match it, or a multi-lot drawdown left short when one lot runs out mid-line.

rules.rule: Invariant 3: a lot's remaining_qty never goes negative and never exceeds its original quantity.
rules.violation: A drawdown with no oversell guard, or a void/restore path returning more units to a lot than it consumed.

rules.rule: Invariant 4: realized P/L across all lines reconciles with the lot cost actually drawn down.
rules.violation: Realized P/L computed from anything but proceeds minus the basis of the lots consumed, or an aggregate that counts a voided line.

rules.rule: Invariant 5: voiding or editing a posted transaction reverses its lot effects atomically — edit is reverse + re-post inside one DB transaction.
rules.violation: A void or edit whose reversal and re-post can commit separately, or a failure path that leaves lots drawn down for a line that is now void.

rules.rule: Invariant 6: per transaction, sum(incoming lot.unit_cost_cents * quantity) equals net_consideration_in, residual absorbed on the largest-value incoming line; the outgoing side reconciles symmetrically against net_consideration_out, with any indivisible per-unit residual absorbed by splitting the out line.
rules.violation: A split whose parts do not re-sum to the total, a dropped or redistributed rounding residual, or an out-line residual handled by anything other than splitting the line.

rules.rule: Invariant 7: every lot has a non-null intent (personal | resale | ripping) and a non-null acquired_market_value_cents.
rules.violation: A lot insert leaving either column NULL, or a migration adding a lot-creating path that does not populate them.

rules.rule: Invariant 8: ripping lots are never consumed by a disposal — they cannot appear on an `out` line — and are always valued at $0 market, so unrealized loss equals cost basis.
rules.violation: An open-lot query for disposal that does not exclude intent 'ripping', or a valuation path pricing a ripping lot above zero.

rules.rule: Invariant 9: a lot flagged `missing` is excluded from on-hand quantity and is never consumed, and is valued at $0 market while keeping its cost basis. Clearing the flag restores it exactly.
rules.violation: An on-hand or disposal query not filtering `missing = 0`, a valuation pricing a missing lot above zero, or an unflag path that does not restore the prior state exactly.

rules.rule: One unified transaction posting algorithm handles purchase/sale/trade; `type` is inferred from which sides carry cards, never passed in by the caller.
rules.violation: A second posting path for one transaction kind, or a caller that decides the type itself instead of letting _infer_type derive it from the give/receive sides.

rules.rule: A SQLite connection belongs to the thread that created it; a worker opens its own.
rules.violation: A connection created on the UI thread and used inside a QThread, or shared across threads.

rules.rule: A running QThread that is garbage-collected aborts the process; workers must be owned and awaited, and deleteLater needs an event loop to take effect.
rules.violation: A worker started without a reference that outlives it, or teardown that relies on deleteLater with no loop running.

rules.rule: Work that blocks a repaint — subprocess, network, model loads, filesystem walks — belongs behind ui/views/_worker.py's TaskWorker.
rules.violation: A subprocess call, httpx request, ONNX session build or directory walk on the UI thread.

rules.rule: A PreToolUse hook fails open on its own confusion and closed only on the condition it actually detected. Unparseable stdin, an unbalanced quote, no git, an unreadable registry: return 0.
rules.violation: A raise, an unguarded parse, or a network call on the hook path — it runs before every shell call, so failing closed on confusion stops all work in the session.

rules.rule: A hook decides what a command does from argv positions via _shell.segments(), never by searching the command text.
rules.violation: A regex over the raw command string to classify an invocation — it is simultaneously too broad (quoted prose matches) and too narrow (a variable or an alias does not).

rules.rule: A running worker is never overwritten. Interrupt and park it with retire(worker, parked) from ui/views/_worker.py, or return early while one is in flight.
rules.violation: Assigning over a worker attribute that may still be running — requestInterruption() followed by a reassignment is the exact shape that aborts the process, since interruption only raises a flag.

rules.rule: Only inventory.db is the ledger; vision.db, auctions.db and pricehistory.db are derived or ephemeral and are not migrated by data/migrator.py.
rules.violation: Treating a derived database as the ledger (or the reverse) — e.g. a numbered migration for vision.db, or ledger data written to auctions.db.

rules.rule: Windows share tables; a change to a shared table or service reaches every window that reads it.
rules.violation: A schema or service change whose other readers — per .claude/context/app-map.json — are not accounted for.

rules.rule: A test must fail if the behaviour it covers regresses; asserting the setup does not count.
rules.violation: A behavioural change with no test that would go red on revert, or a test that passes against a broken implementation.

rules.rule: A new validator, guard, lint or gate ships with a test proving it fails on bad input.
rules.violation: A check subcommand or guard exercised only against the passing case.

rules.rule: Qt tests run offscreen (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen) and the suite runs in parallel with -n auto --dist loadfile; a file's tests share a worker.
rules.violation: A UI test that needs a display, or a test depending on cross-file ordering or module state set elsewhere.

rules.rule: Adding or renaming a window, migration, service or window test updates .claude/context/app-map.json in the same change.
rules.violation: New structure with a stale map — tests/test_app_map.py is where it surfaces.

rules.rule: Never hardcode a colour in a view; read tokens via theme.active().
rules.violation: A hex literal, a named colour, or a stylesheet colour outside ui/theme.py.

rules.rule: money(cents) and percent() in ui/formatting.py are the only place cents become strings.
rules.violation: An f-string or format call turning cents into display text anywhere else.

rules.rule: Inline card rows use ui/views/_card_entry.py — CardEntryMixin, PriceLookupWorker, MatchDelegate. Do not fork it.
rules.violation: A new inline card row with its own autocomplete, pricing or match delegate.

rules.rule: Hover shows the hovered card; on leave fall back to the selected card, else the last hovered.
rules.violation: A preview that clears on leave, or that ignores the selection.

rules.rule: Icons are Lucide SVGs from ui/assets/icons/, tinted at call time via icons.icon(name, color, size).
rules.violation: A QIcon built from a path or resource directly, an emoji or text glyph standing in for an icon, or an icon colour that is not a theme token.

rules.rule: In a Qt model's data(), compare plain ints rather than wrapped enums, answer the sort role first, and cache it per (row, column) cleared in set_rows().
rules.violation: A model whose data() falls through enum comparisons before reaching the sort role, or recomputes the sort key per call.

rules.rule: A real concern this registry does not yet cover. Raise it, never block on it, and say what rule should exist.
rules.violation: n/a — this id exists so a grounded panel can still surface something novel without inventing a mandate.
